clue.text: Daily sex — strangely, that could be a problem

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of daily sex are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style hint that frequent sex might lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nudges towards a moral or medical problem; the real problem is a reading and spelling difficulty, which the setter notes the answer itself is hard to spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a learning difficulty with reading and spelling, so it can be called a problem.

clue.text: Dull squabbles in Dudley on vacation

indicators.note: in says the quarrels go inside the emptied town
on vacation says Dudley is emptied, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: rows are quarrels

explanation.surface: Boring rows in the West Midlands town of Dudley during the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley is a town in the English West Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy means sleepy and sluggish, so dull.

clue.text: Hammer's essentially brass-lined cutting side

indicators.note: essentially points to the central letters of brass-lined, its essence

parts.note: the edge is the cutting side of a blade

explanation.surface: A sledgehammer's head with a brass-lined striking face.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a sledgehammer, a heavy two-handed hammer.

clue.text: Coming onto stage to fill with rapture

definitions.meaning: to delight or enchant, as if putting into a trance

explanation.surface: An actor's appearance captivating the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: EN-trance and en-TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor makes an appearance on stage; to enchant someone is to put them in a trance.

clue.text: Unpleasant daughter leaving in poor condition

indicators.note: leaving says the daughter letter goes out of the word

parts.note: dicky is British slang for weak or unsound, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: A nasty scene as a daughter moves out of a shabby home.
explanation.walkthrough: DICKY is British informal for shaky or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for nasty or distasteful.

clue.text: Graduate cunningly manipulates without spite, possibly

indicators.note: cunningly says the remaining letters are rearranged in a crafty new order
without says the letters of spite are taken away from manipulates
possibly warns that the letters of spite are removed wherever they fall, not as one run

explanation.surface: A former student shrewdly handles people, perhaps without any malice.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike S, P, I, T and E from MANIPULATES, leaving MANULA, and 'cunningly' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student of a school or university, a graduate.

clue.text: Discarding diamonds upset one so old — 27!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the kept letters are read upwards, backwards
discarding diamonds throws away the D at the end of the words; the opening O must go too, so in effect only the letters within are kept, as the setter's revised 'Endlessly' makes plain

explanation.surface: Throwing off diamonds unsettles someone of great age.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, dropping only D from ONESOOLD and reversing gives LOOSENO, one O too many; Big Dave's blog quotes Chalicea's fix, 'Endlessly upset one so old – 27!'. The cross-reference is to 27 down, UNDO.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot is to slacken or release it, the same as loosening.

clue.text: Precise details of humanities sorted out without disheartened heads

indicators.note: sorted out says the remaining letters are put into a new order
without says the head letters are removed from humanities
disheartened says heads loses its middle, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Arts subjects tidied up without dispirited department heads.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H and S from HUMANITIES, then rearrange UMANITIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, exact particulars, the fine points of a matter.

clue.text: Correctness of current church office

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: Getting the details right at a modern parish post.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy is exactness, being correct and free of error.

clue.text: Abruptly come upon evident dark web, ignoring the odds

parts.note: something evident is overt, open to view

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means only the even-placed letters of dark web are kept

explanation.surface: Suddenly stumbling upon the shady hidden internet, despite the chances.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtake can mean to strike or befall someone suddenly, as a storm or disaster does.

clue.text: Insignificant employee with boundless talent produces quality drink

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor worker

indicators.note: boundless says the word for talent loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a knack is a talent or skill

explanation.surface: A lowly worker with endless ability ends up making a fine spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a premium French brandy, a drink of quality.

clue.text: Look closely at wasp, say, gobbling middle of apple

indicators.note: gobbling says the insect word swallows another letter

parts.note: a wasp is an example of an insect

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of apple

explanation.surface: Examine the wasp devouring the core of an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine something carefully.

clue.text: Notable prisoner accepting prison, ultimately, is revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary says the whole assembly turns round and is read backwards
accepting says the prisoner word takes in another letter

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of prison

explanation.surface: A famous convict who takes the jail over at last is a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notable' looks like a noun describing the prisoner; it is the adjective definition, as in a signal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective signal means striking or remarkable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Source of stability getting established for hospital's early version

indicators.note: getting introduces the new piece that comes into the word
for says the new piece stands in place of the hospital letter

parts.note: an anchor keeps a ship steady
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop fronts

explanation.surface: A firm foundation becoming the basis for a hospital's first form.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor can be a forerunner or prototype from which a later thing developed.

clue.text: Excellent sauce

definitions.meaning: a rich white sauce made with chicken stock and cream

explanation.walkthrough: Sauce suprême is a classic French cream sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means best of all; suprême is also a velouté sauce enriched with cream.

clue.text: Crowd gutlessly ply strong brew

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly crowd or crush

indicators.note: gutlessly says ply loses its middle, keeping its outer letters

explanation.surface: A spineless attempt to push strong drink on a throng.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUMPY is rough, strong farmhouse cider from the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is a potent rough cider, a strong brewed drink.

clue.text: Vintner's refuse to hastily swot up about

indicators.note: up about says the swotting word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to study hurriedly before an exam

explanation.surface: A wine merchant declining to do some rushed revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the residue of skins and pips left after grapes are pressed, a winemaker's waste.

clue.text: Malinger in resort just starting up

indicators.note: in resort reads as re-sort, so the letters of malinger are sorted again

explanation.surface: Skiving off at a holiday resort that has only just opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Germinal means in the earliest stage of development, like a sprouting seed.

clue.text: Divulge information about duck theft

indicators.note: about says the informing word goes round the duck

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: Grassing on someone over a stolen duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking another's property, the act of theft.

clue.text: Game with measure of winner's lead for jumper

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
a horse can win a race by a neck

explanation.surface: A sport where a horse wins by a neck, for a showjumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a showjumping horse; in British English it is a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a sweater with a high, folded collar.

clue.text: Is better than not opening items for consumption

indicators.note: not opening says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: beats means is better than

explanation.surface: A claim that something unopened beats food on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, things to be consumed.

clue.text: Piece of land or vehicle working it

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Choosing between a field and the machine that farms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on the first part: the 'it' being worked is the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the farm vehicle that ploughs and works fields.

clue.text: Let it stand framing Royal Engineers' thoroughfare

indicators.note: framing says the proofreading word surrounds the army letters

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Leaving the army engineers' road as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town, a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Scale of a second century death

parts.note: end means death

explanation.surface: A measure of how someone died in the second century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like a noun; here it is the verb, to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to climb up it.

clue.text: Hostile, flexible and strong holding no trumps

indicators.note: holding says the wiry word takes in the bridge letters

parts.note: wiry means lean, tough and supple
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: An unfriendly, tough bridge player holding no trumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry can describe a cold, unfriendly manner, as in a wintry smile.

clue.text: Period intervening in poor sentence

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: Time passing during a shabby spell behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the interval between two events.

clue.text: Good French monkey plant

parts.note: bon is French for good
the sai is a South American capuchin monkey

explanation.surface: A fine French primate as a stooge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' can suggest a planted spy; here it is a miniature tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a dwarfed potted tree, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Let loose gun dog, removing restraints

indicators.note: removing restraints says the phrase gun dog sheds its outer letters, as if unleashed, leaving the letters within

explanation.surface: Unleashing a hunting dog by taking off its leash.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo is to unfasten or release something that was tied.

clue.text: Arrested northern cook on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the cook's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook

explanation.surface: A cook from the north detained while heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a long-standing British television cook, known by first name alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed is slang for caught or arrested by the police.

clue.text: Find stern tests all uncovered concern

indicators.note: all uncovered says each of the three words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Discover that rigorous exams are all exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a stake or concern in something, as in a business interest.

clue.text: Liberal French floor returning ambassador

indicators.note: returning says the French floor word is read backwards

parts.note: étage is French for a floor or storey

explanation.surface: A Liberal envoy heading back across a French storey.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially one representing the Pope.

clue.text: Unremarkable path involving kilometres in tortuous road

indicators.note: involving says the path word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a way is a path

indicators.note: in says the distance letter goes inside the reworked road
tortuous means twisting, so the letters of road are jumbled

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilometres

explanation.surface: A dull route taking in miles of winding road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortuous' jumbles the road letters to ORAD before the kilometres letter goes in, giving ORKAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means ordinary or everyday, nothing special.
